                    new_routes[rj].customers.append(cust)
                    ok, _ = _route_arrival_and_close(inst, new_routes[rj].customers)
                    if ok and sum(cust_by_id[c].demand for c in new_routes[rj].customers) <= inst.vehicle_capacity:
                        new_sol = Solution(inst.instance_id, new_routes, solution.solver, solution.wall_clock_seconds, solution.budget_seconds, False)
                        new_sol.metrics = evaluate(inst, new_sol, context.settings)
                        if new_sol.metrics['feasible'] and new_sol.metrics['operational_cost'] < best_cost:
                            best_cost, best_sol = new_sol.metrics['operational_cost'], new_sol
    return best_sol

rationale: The 'Route-Centroid Swap' operator identifies routes whose geometric centroids are spatially close (using Manhattan distance on coordinate means) and attempts to swap a customer from one to the other. Unlike local search moves that optimize edges, this operator performs a global structural alignment based on spatial clusters, effectively 'untangling' routes that have drifted into each other's geographical territory, which is a common failure mode of greedy insertion.
code:
from __future__ import annotations
import time
from svrptw.config import Settings
from svrptw.council.proposal import OperatorContext
from svrptw.io import Instance
from svrptw.solvers.common import Route, Solution, evaluate
from svrptw.solvers.common.local_search import _cust_by_id

def operator(solution: Solution, context: OperatorContext) -> Solution | None:
    inst, settings = context.instance, context.settings
    cust_by_id = _cust_by_id(inst)
    routes = [r for r in solution.routes if r.customers]
    if len(routes) < 2: return None
    centroids = []
    for r in routes:
        xs = [inst.customers[c-1].x for c in r.customers]
        ys = [inst.customers[c-1].y for c in r.customers]
        centroids.append((sum(xs)/len(xs), sum(ys)/len(ys)))
    for i in range(len(routes)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(routes)):
            dist = abs(centroids[i][0]-centroids[j][0]) + abs(centroids[i][1]-centroids[j][1])
            if dist < 5.0:
                for ci, c_id in enumerate(routes[i].customers):
                    new_routes = [Route(customers=list(r.customers)) for r in solution.routes]
                    new_routes[i].customers.pop(ci)
                    new_routes[j].customers.append(c_id)
                    new_sol = Solution(solution.instance_id, new_routes, solution.solver, solution.wall_clock_seconds, solution.budget_seconds, False)
                    new_sol.metrics = evaluate(inst, new_sol, settings)
                    if new_sol.metrics['feasible'] and new_sol.metrics['operational_cost'] < solution.metrics['operational_cost']:
                        new_sol.feasible = True
                        return new_sol
    return None
